description: Does this evidence actually prove this SOC 2 control operated effectively? Each task presents synthetic evidence artifacts plus a control claim; the model must return a verdict (Sufficient / Insufficient) and a one-line reason. Verdicts are scored exact-match with no partial credit; reason quality is reported separately as a reason-hit rate against per-task anchor terms.
eval_name: SOC 2 Evidence Judgment Eval (micro1 Eval Hackathon)

scoring.note: T4 is scored as two half-verdicts (0.5 per claim).
scoring.reason_hit_rate: Diagnostic only. Fraction of verdict units whose model-supplied reason contains at least one of the unit's anchor terms (case-insensitive substring match). T4 counts as two verdict units (one per claim), so the denominator is 13.

tasks.claim: MFA is enforced for all workforce users (CC6.1).
tasks.key_reason: The tenant-level MFA toggle is ON, but the per-group policy list exempts the Contractors group; 3 of 41 sampled users are contractors, so enforcement is not org-wide.
tasks.title: The plausible screenshot

tasks.claim: Vulnerabilities are scanned weekly and remediated within SLA (CC7.2), observation period Apr 1 - Jun 30, 2026.
tasks.key_reason: The clean scan report is dated Mar 3, 2026, before the Apr 1 - Jun 30 observation period; the scan history shows no scans inside the period (the next scan is Jul 8, after period end), so there is no in-period evidence of weekly scanning.
tasks.title: The stale log

tasks.claim: Access is reviewed quarterly and terminated users are removed promptly (CC6.1).
tasks.key_reason: The user terminated Jun 12, 2026 is still an active IdP account on Jun 30, 18 days later; the review sign-off (Jun 10) predates the termination and covers a stale 38-user population while the IdP lists 39 active accounts.
tasks.title: The access review that misses one

tasks.key_reason: Split verdict: the artifact supports CC6.6 (encryption at rest) but not CC7.2 (monitoring).

subclaims.key_reason: The configuration report directly evidences AES-256 encryption at rest with managed, rotated KMS keys for all production data stores.
An encryption configuration report is not monitoring evidence; it contains no detection, alerting, or anomaly data, so it cannot support CC7.2.

tasks.title: Right artifact, wrong control

tasks.claim: Changes are approved and tested before production (CC8.1).
tasks.key_reason: Ticket CHG-4417 was approved by the requester themselves (no peer approval / segregation of duties), has no testing evidence attached, and used the emergency path with no post-hoc review as the policy requires.
tasks.title: The change ticket

tasks.claim: Vendor monitoring is covered by the vendor's SOC 2 report (CC9.2).
tasks.key_reason: The vendor's clean SOC 2 report carves out the backup subsystem as a carved-out subservice organization, and the in-scope system stores its backups exactly there, so reliance on the report does not cover that risk without complementary controls.
tasks.title: The carve-out gap

tasks.claim: Audit logs are complete and retained (CC7.2), observation period Sep 1 - Sep 30, 2026.
tasks.key_reason: Exports for Sep 14, 15, and 16 are missing from the 30-day set, an unexplained 3-day gap; the admin attestation claiming 'no gaps' contradicts the artifacts.
tasks.title: The gap in the sequence

tasks.claim: MFA is enforced for all workforce users (CC6.1), observation period Jul 1 - Sep 30, 2026.
tasks.key_reason: The enforcement report covers all 41 workforce users with no exemptions, the IdP configuration export is dated inside the observation period, and two sampled login events show MFA challenges, corroborating enforcement.
tasks.title: The one that should pass

tasks.claim: Backups are regularly tested to confirm data can be restored (CC7.4), observation period Jul 1 - Sep 30, 2026.
tasks.key_reason: All 30 nightly backup jobs in the log completed with status Success, but the artifact set contains no restore test record of any kind, while the backup policy requires a documented restore test at least quarterly. Successful backup jobs prove data was copied, not that it can be restored.
tasks.title: Backup success is not a restore test

tasks.claim: Penetration testing is performed at least annually and findings are addressed (CC7.1).
tasks.key_reason: The penetration test was performed in August 2026, maintaining the annual cadence, with scope explicitly covering the production environment; the one critical finding was remediated and confirmed closed on retest, and both medium findings were formally risk-accepted in writing by the CISO with named compensating controls and a scheduled retest date, so every finding is dispositioned.
tasks.title: The second one that should pass

tasks.claim: Logical access controls operated effectively throughout the observation period Oct 1 - Dec 31, 2026 (CC6.1).
tasks.key_reason: The only evidence is a SOC 2 Type I report, which expresses an opinion on the suitability of the design of controls as of a single date (November 15, 2026) and explicitly does not evaluate operating effectiveness over a period. A point-in-time design opinion cannot support a claim that controls operated effectively throughout Oct 1 - Dec 31, 2026; that claim requires a Type II examination.
tasks.title: The wrong report type

tasks.claim: All production changes in Q1 2026 were approved before deployment (CC8.1).
tasks.key_reason: Two of the six changes defeat the claim, visible only by cross-referencing the two logs: CHG-5102 was deployed Mar 9 at 22:40 but its approval is timestamped Mar 10 at 09:00, after deployment; and CHG-5105 was approved by its own requester (self-approval), so it carries no independent approval at all. An approval existing somewhere in the log for every change is not the same as every change being approved before deployment.
tasks.title: Approved on paper
